analysis:
Three changes were reviewed.

1. coordinator/cmd/devnet-seed/seed.go is a new offline seeding tool. It writes straight through store.Store: CreateUser, CreateAPIKey, UpsertProvider, the provider session calls, Credit, Debit, RecordUsage and CreditProviderAccount. It touches the A-009 payment ledger and provider earnings, and mints `LedgerDeposit` credits without any Stripe flow. Seeded data is plainly marked: example.invalid emails, did:privy:seed-N IDs, SEED%08d serials, fake models, TrustLevel "none", backend "devnet-seed", and a provider key derived from a hash of the serial, which is public data rather than a private key. API key values are discarded, so the seeded accounts cannot be used to authenticate. No App Attest, MDM or serving-authorization state is created, so the TB-011 and T-052..T-058 serving paths are unaffected. The tool never touches the network or any trust boundary directly. The residual risk is that if it were pointed at a production DATABASE_URL it would inject fake accounts and ledger money. Any environment guard would live in the sibling main.go/options code, which was not supplied (only seed.go appears in this batch), so I could not verify it. Next pass: check that main.go refuses non-dev or production DSNs and requires explicit confirmation.

2. deploy/gcp/bootstrap.sh changes are comments only (lines 2-30), with no behavioral or security effect.

3. deploy/gcp/vm-startup.sh line 136 adds EIGENINFERENCE_IPAPI_KEY=$(fetch eigeninference-ipapi-key) to the dev env file. The file is written to /etc/d-inference/env with chmod 600 in a 700 directory, matching how other secrets are handled. `fetch` silently tolerates a missing secret. The new secret is not created by bootstrap.sh, which its comment now says explicitly. The coordinator service account already has project-level secretAccessor, so no IAM change is needed. This is dev-only and out of scope per the threat model, and I found no regression.

No findings. needs_deeper_review is true only because the devnet-seed entrypoint and options were not visible.
